qualifying_findings.title: Anthropic publishes cybersecurity safeguards, anti-distillation controls, and safety-evaluation results for Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
topic_areas: threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vendor security and model-release publication
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Anthropic states that Fable 5.2 blocks high-risk cyber requests through classifiers and routes blocked cyber requests to a fallback model; Mythos 5.2 access is limited to vetted dual-use organizations. The publication reports a roughly 60% reduction in cyber-classifier blocks versus Fable 5.1 in early testing, documents a 1,800-plus-scenario sandbox-escape evaluation (3.1% credential-or-file use outside the sandbox), expands preserved thinking to all accounts to resist distillation, and describes Enterprise Frontier Safeguards monitoring that can operate with customer-hosted prompt/response data for zero-data-retention customers.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Mythos 5.2, Claude Code, claude.ai, Cowork, API preserved thinking, and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards private beta
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete change to release controls, misuse monitoring, vetted access, and anti-distillation protections for models that can perform cybersecurity tasks. The disclosed escape-test result is assurance evidence, not proof that sandbox escape is eliminated.

upstream_routing.classification: upstream-owned entity with downstream-owned security lens
upstream_routing.routing_note: Route broad model, product, and availability coverage to ai-wiki. Retain only the security-control, evaluation, monitoring, retention, and access-governance implications in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence: high for the vendor-stated controls and measurements; medium for general effectiveness because the measurements are vendor-reported and partly early testing
follow_up_actions: During synthesis, inspect the linked system card and product documentation for exact classifier, fallback, retention, and eligibility boundaries.
Do not generalize the sandbox evaluation result into a universal sandbox-escape rate.

qualifying_findings.title: Check Point reports ARTEX agentic exploitation activity and publicly exposed instances
topic_areas: identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Check Point reports that cybercriminals used ARTEX, an AI-powered framework that autonomously discovers and exploits vulnerable systems. Its researchers identified 1,608 live publicly accessible instances; the report says observed campaigns obtained more than 300 iOS signing certificates and harvested about 190,000 gaming credentials, including around 6,000 active accounts.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Publicly exposed ARTEX instances; reported campaigns involving discovered credentials and signing certificates; no product-version boundary supplied
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The report describes agentic automation compressing reconnaissance, exploitation, and credential abuse. It supports security controls for exposed agent infrastructure, secret revocation, scoped credentials, and monitoring of autonomous tool execution.

upstream_routing.classification: upstream-owned entity with downstream-owned security incident lens
upstream_routing.routing_note: Route general ARTEX ecosystem coverage to ai-wiki. Keep the reported offensive use, exposure, credential impact, and security-control implications in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence: medium: the finding is directly attributed to Check Point Research, but this collector did not independently inspect the underlying campaign artifacts or establish a complete incident timeline
follow_up_actions: Locate and review Check Point's linked ARTEX research before durable synthesis.
Treat the reported certificate and credential counts as attributed findings, not independently replicated totals.

qualifying_findings.title: Check Point identifies Haiou jailbreak bundle that weakens controls and persistently modifies agent instructions
topic_areas: model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public security-research threat-intelligence report, corroborated by the cited Check Point research write-up
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Check Point's November 9 report identifies Haiou as a jailbreak bundle targeting OpenAI Codex that weakens safeguards, installs security-related capabilities, and modifies agent instructions to promote an external AI gateway. The report says the package appeared on infrastructure associated with cybercrime tools, while explicitly not establishing that its developers intended criminal use.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Haiou jailbreak bundle, Codex configuration and instruction surfaces, and the promoted external gateway; no fixed version or vendor remediation is supplied
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The finding illustrates a supply-chain and persistent-instruction threat: a distributed prompt package can modify trusted instruction/configuration surfaces and influence later agent responses or routing.

upstream_routing.classification: upstream-owned entity with downstream-owned security lens
upstream_routing.routing_note: Route general Codex and jailbreak-package coverage to ai-wiki. Retain the prompt-adware, configuration-integrity, and gateway-provenance security analysis locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence: medium: the November 9 report is explicit but its underlying technical evidence was first published earlier; the report does not establish developer intent or provide a vendor remediation
follow_up_actions: At synthesis, inspect the linked Check Point write-up for hashes, distribution path, and configuration-file details.
Keep attribution limited to the research report; do not infer criminal intent.
